title: Adobe Firefly Content Credentials: Verify C2PA in Files | AICheck365
description: Check Adobe Firefly files for Content Credentials: C2PA manifest, signature and trust state, digitalSourceType and XMP fields — verified against a real Firefly sample.
h1: Adobe Firefly Content Credentials Checker: verify C2PA in the original file
eyebrow: High-intent tool guide · United States / English
lead: Adobe Firefly exports can carry C2PA Content Credentials that record provenance in a signed manifest. AICheck365 checks whether the manifest exists, validates the signature, separates cryptographic validity from trust-list status, and shows digitalSourceType, claim generator, assertions, ingredients, and related XMP fields.

direct.heading: Quick answer: verify the signed manifest before trusting labels
direct.body: A valid manifest that identifies trained algorithmic media is strong evidence that the signed file was produced or edited in an AI workflow. Read signature validity and trust status separately: a cryptographically valid signature may still use a certificate that is not currently in the local trust list.

evidenceRows: Signed provenance record embedded in the original file.
Can declare trainedAlgorithmicMedia or another creation/editing category.
Useful supporting metadata, but not equivalent to a signed manifest.
signalRows: Checks whether the signed claim and asset hashes validate.
Reports whether the signing identity is recognized by the active trust configuration.
Identifies the software or service that created the manifest.
Shows actions, provenance statements, and upstream assets when present.
steps: Use the direct Firefly or Adobe export rather than a screenshot.
Open the C2PA Validator and load the file.
Read manifest presence, signature validity, trust state, digitalSourceType, and claim generator.
Save the raw JSON when the result needs to be audited or reproduced.
limits: Social networks, image editors, and re-exports can remove or replace Content Credentials.
A valid signature proves integrity of the signed claim, not that every visual statement in the image is true.
No manifest in a derivative copy does not rule out a Firefly origin.
faq: Are Adobe Content Credentials the same as a visible watermark?
No. They are machine-readable signed provenance data embedded in or associated with the file.
Why can a signature be valid but not trusted?
The cryptography can validate while the signer is absent from the current local trust list.
